source.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν προπάτορα ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα;

records.literal_gloss: What then will we say to have found Abraham the forefather of us according to flesh?

en.L: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather according to [the] flesh, has found?
en.B: What then are we to say that Abraham, our ancestor by natural descent, has found?
en.R: Think about Abraham, the ancestor of the Jewish people. What did he find out about being right with God?

es.L: ¿Qué diremos, pues, que ha encontrado Abraham, nuestro antepasado según [la] carne?
es.B: ¿Qué hemos de decir, entonces, que descubrió Abraham, nuestro antepasado por descendencia natural?
es.R: Pensemos en Abraham, el antepasado del pueblo judío. ¿Qué descubrió él sobre cómo estar en una relación correcta con Dios?

sw.L: Basi tutasema Ibrahimu, babu yetu kwa kadiri ya mwili, amepata nini?
sw.B: Basi, tuseme Ibrahimu, babu yetu kwa ukoo wa kimwili, aligundua nini?
sw.R: Mfikirie Ibrahimu, babu wa Wayahudi. Aligundua nini kuhusu kuwa na uhusiano mwema na Mungu?

fr.L: Que dirons-nous donc qu’Abraham, notre ancêtre selon [la] chair, a trouvé ?
fr.B: Que dirons-nous donc qu’Abraham, notre ancêtre par la naissance, a découvert ?
fr.R: Pensez à Abraham, l’ancêtre du peuple juif. Qu’a-t-il découvert sur la façon d’être juste aux yeux de Dieu ?

decisions.reason: Abraham was honored as the father of the Jewish people. Paul, a Jew, says "our forefather according to the flesh"; from verse 11 he shows that Abraham is father in a wider sense too.

decisions.choice: one question: what did Abraham find?
alternatives: two questions: "What then shall we say? Have we found Abraham to be our forefather according to the flesh?"
decisions.reason: The Greek can also be divided into two questions, asking whether believers, Jew and Gentile, belong to Abraham's family by natural descent. The question about what Abraham found fits verse 2, which asks how he was declared righteous.

decisions.choice: "has found" stands in the text, after "say"
alternatives: some manuscripts put "has found" after "Abraham" or "our forefather"
at least one important early manuscript leaves it out
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "has found" after "what then shall we say". (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)
Readable says what the question is about, which verse 2 makes clear.

decisions.choice: kwa kadiri ya mwili (L); kwa ukoo wa kimwili (B)
decisions.reason: Here the flesh is plain physical descent (meaning decision), not human nature set against the Spirit, so Swahili keeps "mwili" and does not use "asili ya dhambi". Balanced says "kwa ukoo wa kimwili" (by bodily lineage), as the English Balanced says "by natural descent". The question stays one question, as the meaning decision reads it.

decisions.choice: kuhusu kuwa na uhusiano mwema na Mungu
decisions.reason: Readable says what the question is about, as the English Readable does, in the words Romans 3:21 and 9:30 use for being right with God.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἔχει καύχημα· ἀλλ’ οὐ πρὸς θεόν, τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει;

records.literal_gloss: If for Abraham by works was justified, he has a boast; but not toward God. \v 3 What for the Scripture says?

en.L: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has a boast, but not before God. \v 3 For what does the Scripture say?
en.B: Suppose Abraham was declared righteous because of his works: then he would have grounds for boasting, but not in God's presence. \v 3 What does Scripture say?
en.R: If Abraham had been made right with God because of the good things he did, he would have something to be proud of. But he could not be proud in front of God. \v 3 Look at what the Scriptures say:

es.L: Porque si Abraham fue justificado por [las] obras, tiene [motivo de] jactancia, pero no ante Dios. \v 3 Porque ¿qué dice la Escritura?
es.B: Supongamos que Abraham fue justificado por sus obras: entonces tendría motivo para jactarse, pero no delante de Dios. \v 3 ¿Qué dice la Escritura?
es.R: Si Abraham hubiera sido declarado justo por las cosas buenas que hizo, tendría algo de qué jactarse. Pero no podría jactarse delante de Dios. \v 3 Esto es lo que dicen las Escrituras:

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa Ibrahimu alihesabiwa haki kwa matendo, anayo [sababu ya] kujivuna, lakini si mbele za Mungu. \v 3 Kwa maana Maandiko yanasema nini?
sw.B: Tuseme Ibrahimu alihesabiwa haki kwa sababu ya matendo yake: basi angekuwa na sababu ya kujivuna, lakini si mbele za Mungu. \v 3 Maandiko yanasema nini?
sw.R: Kama Ibrahimu angehesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa sababu ya mambo mema aliyoyafanya, angekuwa na kitu cha kujivunia. Lakini hangeweza kujivuna mbele za Mungu. \v 3 Hivi ndivyo Maandiko yanavyosema:

fr.L: Car si Abraham a été justifié par les œuvres, il a de quoi se vanter, mais pas devant Dieu. \v 3 Car que dit l’Écriture ?
fr.B: Supposons qu’Abraham ait été justifié à cause de ses œuvres : il aurait alors de quoi se vanter, mais pas devant Dieu. \v 3 Que dit l’Écriture ?
fr.R: Si Abraham avait été déclaré juste à cause des bonnes choses qu’il avait faites, il aurait eu de quoi être fier. Mais il n’aurait pas pu être fier devant Dieu. \v 3 Regardez ce que disent les Écritures :

decisions.reason: Jewish writings of the time held Abraham up as faithful in testing. 1 Maccabees 2:52 asks, "Was not Abraham found faithful when tested, and it was counted to him as righteousness?", linking Genesis 15:6 to the sacrifice of Isaac (Genesis 22). Paul goes back to Genesis 15 itself.

decisions.choice: but not before God: he has no boast where it counts
alternatives: he could boast before people but not before God
decisions.reason: Paul grants the "if" for the sake of argument, then denies it where it matters: before God Abraham has nothing to boast of, as Scripture shows.

decisions.choice: declared righteous / made right with God
decisions.reason: As in 2:13 and 3:24.

alternatives: puesto en una relación correcta con Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As settled at 2:13 and used in 3:24-30, Literal and Balanced keep "justificar" and Readable says "declarar justo", which keeps the verdict the word describes.

The word for boasting is the one of 3:27, and Spanish keeps the same word as there, "jactancia" and "jactarse", at every level, so the reader sees that Abraham is the test case for 3:27. "Gloriarse", the older wording, could be confused with "gloria" in verse 20.

decisions.choice: alihesabiwa haki (L, B); angehesabiwa haki na Mungu (R)
alternatives: angewekwa katika uhusiano mwema na Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: As settled at 2:13, "kuhesabiwa haki" is kept at every level; Readable adds "na Mungu" where the English Readable says "made right with God". "Kujivuna" (to boast) is the word of 3:27.
As settled at 2:13 and used in 3:20-30: Literal and Balanced keep 'justifier', and Readable says 'déclarer juste', the verdict the word describes.

source.text: Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.

records.literal_gloss: Believed and Abraham the God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.

en.L: "And Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness."
en.B: "Abraham believed God, and that was counted to him as righteousness."
en.R: "Abraham believed God, and God counted that as righteousness."

es.L: «Y creyó Abraham a Dios, y le fue acreditado como justicia».
es.B: «Abraham creyó a Dios, y eso se le acreditó como justicia».
es.R: «Abraham creyó a Dios, y Dios le acreditó esa fe como justicia».

sw.L: "Naye Ibrahimu alimwamini Mungu, na [hilo] likahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki."
sw.B: "Ibrahimu alimwamini Mungu, na hilo likahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki."
sw.R: "Ibrahimu alimwamini Mungu, na Mungu akalihesabu hilo kuwa haki."

fr.L: « Or Abraham a cru Dieu, et cela lui a été compté comme justice. »
fr.B: « Abraham a cru Dieu, et cela lui a été compté comme justice. »
fr.R: « Abraham a cru Dieu, et Dieu a compté cela comme justice. »

decisions.reason: The quotation is Genesis 15:6, in the wording of the Greek translation. In Genesis it follows God's promise that Abraham's offspring would be as many as the stars. Paul quotes it again in Galatians 3:6.
λογίζομαι is a bookkeeping word: to put something to someone's account. Verse 4 uses it of wages. God put righteousness to Abraham's account when he believed.
λογίζομαι comes eleven times in this chapter. The same English is kept wherever it can be, so that the thread of Paul's argument stays visible, as in 9:8.
Readable names God as the one who counts.

Genesis 15:6 is quoted in the same words as Galatians 3:6 and James 2:23, so the reader can see that it is one verse. "Acreditar" is the Spanish bookkeeping word for entering something to a person's account, the sense of the meaning decision; "imputar" now usually means charging someone with a crime. The verb returns ten more times in this chapter, and Spanish keeps "acreditar" wherever something is credited (verses 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 22, 23, 24). Where a sin is counted against someone (verse 8) it says "tomar en cuenta", and Readable says "considerar justo" where a person is counted as righteous.

decisions.choice: [hilo] likahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki (L); hilo likahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki (B); Mungu akalihesabu hilo kuwa haki (R)
decisions.reason: As in James 2:23, Genesis 15:6 is rendered with "-hesabu" and "kuwa haki", and Literal brackets the subject "[hilo]" (that, his believing) that Swahili needs. "Akahesabiwa haki" would be the settled phrase for "was justified"; keeping "kuhesabiwa ... kuwa haki" lets the reader hear the link Paul draws between the two, which runs through the chapter. The verb "-hesabu" is kept for every occurrence of this word in the chapter. Readable names God as the one who counts, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: compter (for the whole chapter, every level)
decisions.reason: The verb is a bookkeeping word, to enter in an account (meaning decision), and Paul uses it eleven times in this chapter. French 'compter' keeps that sense ('compter comme', 'compter à quelqu'un') and is plain enough to stay the same at every level, so the repetition can be followed; 'imputer' is the older theological term but is not everyday French.

decisions.choice: a cru, a été compté (passé composé)
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:6 tells a past event, but Paul quotes it in the middle of his argument to the readers, so French keeps the passé composé used throughout the letter (see 1:1).

source.text: τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα·

records.literal_gloss: To the [one] but working the wage not is counted according to grace but according to debt;

en.L: Now to the one who works, the wage is not counted as a matter of grace but as a debt;
en.B: A worker's wages are not counted as grace but as what is owed.
en.R: When people work, their pay is not a gift of grace. It is what they have earned.

es.L: Ahora bien, al que trabaja, el salario no se le acredita como gracia, sino como deuda;
es.B: Al trabajador, su salario no se le acredita como gracia, sino como algo que se le debe.
es.R: Cuando alguien trabaja, su paga no es un regalo de la gracia. Es lo que se ha ganado.

sw.L: Basi kwa yule anayefanya kazi, mshahara hauhesabiwi kwa kadiri ya neema, bali kwa kadiri ya deni;
sw.B: Mshahara wa mfanyakazi hauhesabiwi kuwa neema, bali kuwa deni analostahili kulipwa.
sw.R: Mtu anapofanya kazi, mshahara wake si zawadi ya neema. Ni malipo aliyoyastahili.

fr.L: Or à celui qui travaille, le salaire n’est pas compté comme une grâce, mais comme une dette ;
fr.B: Le salaire d’un travailleur ne lui est pas compté comme une grâce, mais comme un dû.
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un travaille, son salaire n’est pas un don de la grâce. C’est ce qu’il a gagné.

decisions.reason: μισθός is pay for work; ὀφείλημα is what is owed. A worker's pay is the employer's obligation, not a favor.
Grace here is a gift given freely, the opposite of what is owed.
λογίζομαι comes eleven times in this chapter. The same English is kept wherever it can be, so that the thread of Paul's argument stays visible, as in 9:8.
"Deni" alone is usually heard as what a person owes, but here it is what is owed to the worker (meaning decision). Balanced says "a debt he is entitled to be paid"; Literal keeps the bare "deni".

source.text: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ, πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην, καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων·

records.literal_gloss: to the [one] but not working, believing but on the [one] justifying the ungodly, is counted the faith of him for righteousness, \v 6 just as also David speaks the blessedness of the man to whom the God counts righteousness apart from works;

en.L: but to the one who does not work but believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, {{gender:their|his}} faith is counted as righteousness, \v 6 just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the {{gender:person|man}} to whom God counts righteousness apart from works:
en.B: But to someone who does no work, yet believes in the God who declares the ungodly righteous, that faith is counted as righteousness. \v 6 David says the same when he speaks of the happiness of the one whom God counts as righteous apart from works:
en.R: But some people do not work to earn it. They simply believe in God, who makes ungodly people right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. God counts their faith as righteousness. \v 6 David said the same thing. He talked about how happy people are when God counts them as righteous without their doing anything to earn it.

es.L: pero al que no trabaja, sino que cree en el que justifica al impío, su fe se le acredita como justicia, \v 6 así como también David habla de la bienaventuranza {{gender:del ser humano|del hombre}} a quien Dios acredita justicia aparte de [las] obras:
es.B: Pero al que no trabaja, y sin embargo cree en el Dios que justifica al impío, esa fe se le acredita como justicia. \v 6 David dice lo mismo cuando habla de la dicha de aquel a quien Dios acredita justicia sin las obras:
es.R: Pero hay quienes no trabajan para ganárselo. Simplemente creen en Dios, que declara justos a los impíos. Dios les acredita su fe como justicia. \v 6 David dijo lo mismo. Habló de lo dichosas que son las personas a quienes Dios considera justas sin que hayan hecho nada para ganárselo.

sw.L: lakini kwa yule asiyefanya kazi, bali anamwamini yule anayemhesabia haki asiyemcha Mungu, imani yake inahesabiwa kuwa haki, \v 6 kama vile Daudi pia anavyotaja heri ya mtu ambaye Mungu anamhesabia haki bila matendo:
sw.B: Lakini kwa mtu asiyefanya kazi, ila anamwamini Mungu anayemhesabia haki mtu asiyemcha Mungu, imani hiyo inahesabiwa kuwa haki. \v 6 Daudi anasema vivyo hivyo anapozungumza juu ya furaha ya mtu ambaye Mungu anamhesabu kuwa mwenye haki bila matendo:
sw.R: Lakini watu wengine hawafanyi kazi ili kuipata. Wanamwamini tu Mungu, ambaye huwahesabia haki hata watu wasiomcha. Mungu anaihesabu imani yao kuwa haki. \v 6 Daudi alisema jambo hilo hilo. Alizungumza juu ya furaha waliyo nayo watu ambao Mungu anawahesabu kuwa wenye haki bila wao kufanya lolote ili kuistahili.

fr.L: mais à celui qui ne travaille pas, mais qui croit en celui qui justifie l’impie, sa foi est comptée comme justice, \v 6 comme David aussi parle de la béatitude de {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} à qui Dieu compte la justice sans les œuvres :
fr.B: Mais à celui qui ne travaille pas, et qui pourtant croit en Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui justifie l’impie, cette foi est comptée comme justice. \v 6 David dit la même chose quand il parle du bonheur de celui que Dieu compte comme juste sans les œuvres :
fr.R: Mais certains ne travaillent pas pour le gagner. Ils croient simplement en Dieu, qui déclare justes même les gens qui ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respectent pas. Dieu compte leur foi comme justice. \v 6 David a dit la même chose. Il a parlé du bonheur des gens que Dieu considère comme justes sans qu’ils aient rien fait pour le mériter.

decisions.reason: The law forbade judges to acquit the guilty (Exodus 23:7, Proverbs 17:15). Paul says that God does declare the ungodly righteous, and 3:25-26 has shown how he can do so and still be just.
μακαρισμός is a pronouncement that someone is blessed, as the psalm does in the next verses.

decisions.choice: David: the psalm is headed "Of David"
decisions.reason: Psalm 32, quoted next, bears David's name in its heading.
The words mean any person who believes, man or woman.

decisions.choice: the God who declares the ungodly righteous
alternatives: the one who justifies the ungodly
decisions.reason: Balanced names God, who is meant.
λογίζομαι comes eleven times in this chapter. The same English is kept wherever it can be, so that the thread of Paul's argument stays visible, as in 9:8.

decisions.choice: su fe, no setting; {{gender:del ser humano|del hombre}}
decisions.reason: Spanish "su" means his or her, so the possessive needs no gender span. For the person, Spanish follows the English setting, and "el ser humano" rather than "la persona" keeps the relative "a quien" the same in both options, as in 3:28.

Readable says "declarar justo" for the verb "justify", as settled at 2:13, and "considerar justo" where God counts a person as righteous, which is plainer than crediting righteousness to someone. It keeps "acreditar" where faith is credited, as in the quotation.

decisions.choice: anayemhesabia haki (v. 5); Mungu anamhesabia haki (v. 6, L)
decisions.reason: In Swahili "kumhesabia mtu haki" is both the settled phrase for "justify" and, word for word, "to count righteousness to someone", the wording of verse 6. Paul's argument treats the two as one, so Literal lets them coincide. Balanced and Readable say "anamhesabu kuwa mwenye haki" (counts him as righteous) in verse 6, which makes the bookkeeping picture plain. "Mtu" (a person) needs no gender setting.
French 'sa' agrees with 'foi' and says nothing about the person's sex, so the possessive needs no gender span (see 2:6). For the person, French follows the English setting, as in 3:28.

source.text: Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, μακάριος ἀνὴρ οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [are those] whose were forgiven the lawless deeds and whose were covered the sins; \v 8 blessed man of whom not not will count Lord sin.

en.L: "Blessed [are those] whose lawless deeds were forgiven and whose sins were covered; \v 8 blessed [is the] {{gender:person|man}} whose sin [the] Lord will never count."
en.B: "How happy are those whose wrongs are forgiven, whose sins are covered over! \v 8 How happy is the one whose sin the Lord will never count against them!"
en.R: "How happy are the people whose wrongs God has forgiven, whose sins {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has covered! \v 8 How happy is the person whose sin the Lord will never hold against them!"

es.L: «Bienaventurados [aquellos] cuyas maldades fueron perdonadas y cuyos pecados quedaron cubiertos; \v 8 bienaventurado {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} cuyo pecado [el] Señor jamás tomará en cuenta».
es.B: «¡Qué dichosos son aquellos cuyas faltas son perdonadas, cuyos pecados quedan cubiertos! \v 8 ¡Qué dichoso es aquel a quien el Señor nunca le tomará en cuenta su pecado!»
es.R: «¡Qué felices son las personas a quienes Dios ha perdonado sus faltas y ha cubierto sus pecados! \v 8 ¡Qué feliz es la persona a quien el Señor nunca le pedirá cuentas por su pecado!»

sw.L: "Heri [wale] ambao maasi yao yamesamehewa, na ambao dhambi zao zimefunikwa; \v 8 heri [ni] mtu ambaye dhambi yake Bwana hataihesabu kamwe."
sw.B: "Wana furaha kweli wale ambao maovu yao yamesamehewa, ambao dhambi zao zimefunikwa! \v 8 Ana furaha kweli mtu ambaye Bwana hatamhesabia dhambi yake kamwe!"
sw.R: "Wana furaha kubwa watu ambao Mungu amewasamehe maovu yao na kuzifunika dhambi zao! \v 8 Ana furaha kubwa mtu ambaye Bwana hatamhesabia dhambi yake kamwe!"

fr.L: « Bienheureux ceux dont les iniquités ont été pardonnées et dont les péchés ont été couverts ; \v 8 bienheureux {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} à qui [le] Seigneur ne comptera jamais [le] péché. »
fr.B: « Heureux ceux dont les fautes sont pardonnées, dont les péchés sont couverts ! \v 8 Heureux celui à qui le Seigneur ne comptera jamais son péché ! »
fr.R: « Quel bonheur pour ceux dont Dieu a pardonné les fautes, ceux dont {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a couvert les péchés ! \v 8 Quel bonheur pour celui à qui le Seigneur ne reprochera jamais son péché ! »

decisions.reason: The quotation is Psalm 32:1-2, in the wording of the Greek translation. Where the Greek has "Lord", the Hebrew has God's name, YHWH. The psalm uses the same verb, "count", as Genesis 15:6.
Sins covered are sins God no longer looks on to judge, the language of atonement.
οὐ μὴ together is the strongest denial Greek has.
The word means happy, fortunate, in God's favor. Literal keeps "blessed".
The psalm speaks of anyone, man or woman.
Readable uses the plainest English for counting a sin against someone.
Literal keeps "bienaventurado", as in 14:22. Balanced and Readable follow the English "How happy" with the everyday words for being happy and fortunate.
Spanish follows the English setting, as in verse 6 and 3:28.

decisions.choice: tomar en cuenta (L, B); pedir cuentas (R)
decisions.reason: "Acreditar" puts something to a person's credit; a sin is counted against someone, and Spanish says "tomar en cuenta" for that. It still belongs to the language of accounts, so the link with the other verses of counting stays. Readable says "pedir cuentas" (call to account), as the English Readable says "hold against them".

decisions.choice: Heri (L); Wana furaha kweli (B); Wana furaha kubwa (R); maasi (L), maovu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "heri", as in 14:22. Balanced and Readable follow the English "How happy" with plain words for being happy. The first noun is lawlessness: Literal says "maasi" (acts of rebellion against the law), Balanced and Readable "maovu" (wrongs). "Makosa" is kept for "trespasses" in verse 25. "Mtu" needs no gender setting.

The psalm uses the verb of Genesis 15:6 (meaning decision), so Swahili keeps "-hesabu". "Kumhesabia mtu dhambi" (to count sin to someone) is the opposite of "kumhesabia haki", and is plain enough that Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "hold against them".

Literal keeps 'bienheureux', the traditional word for this psalm blessing; Balanced and Readable say 'heureux' and 'quel bonheur', as the English says 'How happy'. 'Le bonheur' renders the related noun in verses 6 and 9 at Balanced and Readable, 'la béatitude' at Literal.
French follows the English setting at Literal; Balanced and Readable say 'celui', which already means anyone, and 'son péché', whose possessive agrees with 'péché', so they need no span.
A sin is counted against someone; Readable says 'reprocher', as the English Readable says 'hold against them'. Literal and Balanced keep 'compter', the verb of the whole chapter.

source.text: Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν;

records.literal_gloss: The blessedness then this on the circumcision or also on the uncircumcision?

en.L: Is this blessedness then [pronounced] on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised?
en.B: Is this blessing, then, only for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised?
en.R: Is this happiness only for Jews, who are circumcised? Or is it also for people who are not circumcised?

es.L: ¿Es, pues, esta bienaventuranza [pronunciada] sobre los circuncidados, o también sobre los incircuncisos?
es.B: ¿Es esta dicha, entonces, solo para los circuncidados, o también para los incircuncisos?
es.R: ¿Es esta felicidad solo para los judíos, que están circuncidados? ¿O es también para los que no están circuncidados?

sw.L: Basi, je, heri hii [imetamkwa] juu ya waliotahiriwa, au pia juu ya wasiotahiriwa?
sw.B: Je, basi, baraka hii ni kwa ajili ya waliotahiriwa tu, au pia kwa ajili ya wasiotahiriwa?
sw.R: Je, furaha hii ni kwa Wayahudi tu, ambao wametahiriwa? Au ni pia kwa watu ambao hawajatahiriwa?

fr.L: Cette béatitude [est-elle] donc pour les circoncis, ou aussi pour les incirconcis ?
fr.B: Ce bonheur est-il donc seulement pour les circoncis, ou aussi pour les incirconcis ?
fr.R: Ce bonheur est-il seulement pour les Juifs, qui sont circoncis ? Ou est-il aussi pour ceux qui ne sont pas circoncis ?

decisions.choice: the circumcised and the uncircumcised: Jews and Gentiles
decisions.reason: As in 3:30.

source.text: λέγομεν γάρ· Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην.

records.literal_gloss: We say for: was counted to the Abraham the faith for righteousness.

en.L: For we say, "Faith was counted to Abraham as righteousness."
en.B: We have been saying that Abraham's faith was counted to him as righteousness.
en.R: We have said that God counted Abraham's faith as righteousness.

es.L: Porque decimos: «A Abraham le fue acreditada la fe como justicia».
es.B: Hemos venido diciendo que a Abraham su fe se le acreditó como justicia.
es.R: Ya hemos dicho que Dios le acreditó a Abraham su fe como justicia.

sw.L: Kwa maana tunasema, "Imani ilihesabiwa kwa Ibrahimu kuwa haki."
sw.B: Tumekuwa tukisema kwamba imani ya Ibrahimu ilihesabiwa kwake kuwa haki.
sw.R: Tumesema kwamba Mungu aliihesabu imani ya Ibrahimu kuwa haki.

fr.L: Car nous disons : « La foi a été comptée à Abraham comme justice. »
fr.B: Nous l’avons dit : la foi d’Abraham lui a été comptée comme justice.
fr.R: Nous avons dit que Dieu a compté la foi d’Abraham comme justice.

decisions.reason: λογίζομαι comes eleven times in this chapter. The same English is kept wherever it can be, so that the thread of Paul's argument stays visible, as in 9:8.

source.text: πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη;

records.literal_gloss: How then was it counted?

en.L: How then was it counted?
en.B: Under what circumstances, then, was it counted?
en.R: When did God count it?

es.L: ¿Cómo, pues, le fue acreditada?
es.B: ¿En qué circunstancias, entonces, se le acreditó?
es.R: ¿Cuándo se la acreditó Dios?

sw.L: Basi ilihesabiwaje?
sw.B: Basi, ilihesabiwa katika hali gani?
sw.R: Mungu aliihesabu lini?

fr.L: Comment donc a-t-elle été comptée ?
fr.B: Dans quelles circonstances, alors, a-t-elle été comptée ?
fr.R: Quand est-ce que Dieu l’a comptée ?

source.text: ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ;

records.literal_gloss: In circumcision being or in uncircumcision?

en.L: When he was in circumcision or in uncircumcision?
en.B: Was it after he was circumcised, or before?
en.R: Was it after Abraham was circumcised, or before?

es.L: ¿Estando en circuncisión o en incircuncisión?
es.B: ¿Fue después de que él se circuncidara, o antes?
es.R: ¿Fue después de que Abraham fue circuncidado, o antes?

sw.L: Alipokuwa katika tohara au katika kutotahiriwa?
sw.B: Je, ilikuwa baada ya yeye kutahiriwa, au kabla?
sw.R: Je, ilikuwa baada ya Ibrahimu kutahiriwa, au kabla?

fr.L: Alors qu’il était dans la circoncision, ou dans l’incirconcision ?
fr.B: Était-ce après sa circoncision, ou avant ?
fr.R: Était-ce après qu’Abraham a été circoncis, ou avant ?

source.text: οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: Not in circumcision but in uncircumcision;

en.L: Not in circumcision but in uncircumcision;
en.B: It was not after, but before.
en.R: It was before he was circumcised.

es.L: No en circuncisión, sino en incircuncisión;
es.B: No fue después, sino antes.
es.R: Fue antes de que lo circuncidaran.

sw.L: Si katika tohara, bali katika kutotahiriwa;
sw.B: Haikuwa baada, bali kabla.
sw.R: Ilikuwa kabla hajatahiriwa.

fr.L: Non dans la circoncision, mais dans l’incirconcision ;
fr.B: Ce n’était pas après, mais avant.
fr.R: C’était avant qu’il soit circoncis.

decisions.reason: Abraham's faith is counted as righteousness in Genesis 15:6; he is circumcised in Genesis 17. Ishmael's birth falls between: Abraham was 86 then and 99 when he was circumcised (Genesis 16:16, 17:24).

source.text: καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς, σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων δι’ ἀκροβυστίας, εἰς τὸ λογισθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην, καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ.

records.literal_gloss: And sign he received of circumcision, seal of the righteousness of the faith the [one] in the uncircumcision, for the to be him father of all the [ones] believing through uncircumcision, for the to be counted to them the righteousness, \v 12 and father of circumcision to those not from circumcision only but also to those walking in the steps of the in uncircumcision faith of the father of us Abraham.

en.L: And he received [the] sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith [that he had] while uncircumcised, so that he would be [the] father of all who believe while uncircumcised, so that righteousness would be counted to them, \v 12 and [the] father of [the] circumcised, to those who are not only of [the] circumcision but who also walk in the steps of the faith that our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.
en.B: Circumcision was given to him afterward as a sign, a seal on the righteousness that was already his by faith before he was circumcised. In this way he is father to everyone who believes without being circumcised, so that righteousness is counted to them. \v 12 And he is father to the circumcised as well: not to those who are merely circumcised, but to those who walk the same road of faith our father Abraham walked while still uncircumcised.
en.R: Later God gave Abraham circumcision as a sign. It was like a seal to show that God had already counted him as righteous because of his faith, before he was circumcised. So Abraham is the father of everyone who believes, even if they are not circumcised. God counts them as righteous. \v 12 Abraham is also the father of people who are circumcised. But it is not only because they are circumcised. They must also live by faith, as our father Abraham did before he was circumcised.

es.L: Y recibió [la] señal de la circuncisión como sello de la justicia de la fe [que tenía] en la incircuncisión, para que fuera padre de todos los que creen estando incircuncisos, a fin de que se les acreditara la justicia, \v 12 y padre de [los] circuncidados, de los que no solo son de [la] circuncisión, sino que también caminan en las huellas de la fe que nuestro padre Abraham [tenía] estando incircunciso.
es.B: La circuncisión se le dio después como señal, un sello sobre la justicia que ya era suya por la fe antes de ser circuncidado. Así es padre de todos los que creen sin estar circuncidados, para que se les acredite la justicia. \v 12 Y es también padre de los circuncidados: no de los que solo están circuncidados, sino de los que recorren el mismo camino de fe que recorrió nuestro padre Abraham cuando aún no estaba circuncidado.
es.R: Más tarde Dios le dio a Abraham la circuncisión como señal. Era como un sello para mostrar que Dios ya lo consideraba justo por su fe, antes de que fuera circuncidado. Así que Abraham es el padre de todos los que creen, aunque no estén circuncidados. Dios los considera justos. \v 12 Abraham es también el padre de los que están circuncidados. Pero no es solo porque estén circuncidados. También tienen que vivir por la fe, como vivió nuestro padre Abraham cuando aún no estaba circuncidado.

sw.L: Naye alipokea ishara ya tohara kuwa muhuri wa haki ya imani [aliyokuwa nayo] katika kutotahiriwa, ili yeye awe baba wa wote wanaoamini wakiwa hawajatahiriwa, ili haki ihesabiwe kwao, \v 12 na baba wa waliotahiriwa, kwa wale ambao si wa tohara tu, bali pia wanatembea katika hatua za imani ya baba yetu Ibrahimu, imani aliyokuwa nayo akiwa hajatahiriwa.
sw.B: Tohara ilitolewa kwake baadaye kama ishara, muhuri juu ya haki ambayo tayari ilikuwa yake kwa imani kabla hajatahiriwa. Kwa njia hii yeye ni baba wa kila mtu anayeamini bila kutahiriwa, ili haki ihesabiwe kwao. \v 12 Naye ni baba wa waliotahiriwa pia: si wa wale waliotahiriwa tu, bali wa wale wanaotembea katika njia ile ile ya imani ambayo baba yetu Ibrahimu aliitembea alipokuwa bado hajatahiriwa.
sw.R: Baadaye Mungu alimpa Ibrahimu tohara kuwa ishara. Ilikuwa kama muhuri wa kuonyesha kwamba Mungu alikuwa amekwisha kumhesabu kuwa mwenye haki kwa sababu ya imani yake, kabla hajatahiriwa. Kwa hiyo Ibrahimu ni baba wa kila mtu anayeamini, hata kama hajatahiriwa. Mungu anawahesabu kuwa wenye haki. \v 12 Ibrahimu pia ni baba wa watu waliotahiriwa. Lakini si kwa sababu tu wametahiriwa. Ni lazima pia waishi kwa imani, kama baba yetu Ibrahimu alivyoishi kabla hajatahiriwa.

fr.L: Et il a reçu [le] signe de [la] circoncision comme sceau de la justice de la foi [qu’il avait] quand il était incirconcis, afin d’être [le] père de tous ceux qui croient en étant incirconcis, pour que la justice leur soit comptée, \v 12 et [le] père des circoncis, de ceux qui non seulement sont de [la] circoncision, mais qui aussi marchent sur les traces de la foi qu’avait notre père Abraham quand il était incirconcis.
fr.B: La circoncision lui a été donnée ensuite comme signe, comme sceau de la justice qui était déjà la sienne par la foi avant qu’il soit circoncis. Ainsi, il est le père de tous ceux qui croient sans être circoncis, pour que la justice leur soit comptée. \v 12 Il est aussi le père des circoncis : non pas de ceux qui sont seulement circoncis, mais de ceux qui suivent le même chemin de foi que notre père Abraham a suivi alors qu’il n’était pas encore circoncis.
fr.R: Plus tard, Dieu a donné à Abraham la circoncision comme signe. C’était comme un sceau pour montrer que Dieu l’avait déjà compté comme juste à cause de sa foi, avant qu’il soit circoncis. Ainsi, Abraham est le père de tous ceux qui croient, même s’ils ne sont pas circoncis. Dieu les compte comme justes. \v 12 Abraham est aussi le père de ceux qui sont circoncis. Mais pas seulement parce qu’ils sont circoncis. Ils doivent aussi vivre par la foi, comme notre père Abraham l’a fait avant d’être circoncis.

decisions.reason: Genesis 17:11 calls circumcision "the sign of the covenant". A seal confirms that a document is genuine; circumcision confirmed a righteousness Abraham already had.

decisions.choice: one group: circumcised people who also share Abraham's faith
alternatives: two groups: the circumcised, and those who follow Abraham's faith
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats the article before "walk", which could suggest two groups, but the sense requires one: Abraham is father to Jews who are circumcised and also believe.

decisions.choice: "so that righteousness would be counted to them"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has no "also" here. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: walk in the steps: follow the example
decisions.reason: στοιχέω is to walk in line, keep in step; Abraham went ahead, and others follow the path he took.
λογίζομαι comes eleven times in this chapter. The same English is kept wherever it can be, so that the thread of Paul's argument stays visible, as in 9:8.
Readable says who gave the sign and when.

decisions.choice: caminan en las huellas (L); recorren el mismo camino (B)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures walking in line behind someone (meaning decision). Literal keeps the picture of footprints; Balanced says that they travel the same road Abraham travelled, as the English Balanced does.

The Greek says that righteousness is counted to them, the bookkeeping word of the chapter, not the verb "justify". "Ili wahesabiwe haki" would read as the settled phrase for being justified, so Swahili keeps righteousness as the subject: "so that righteousness may be counted to them".

decisions.choice: marchent sur les traces (L); suivent le même chemin (B)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures walking in line behind someone (meaning decision). Literal keeps the picture of footsteps; Balanced says that they travel the same road Abraham travelled, as the English does.

source.text: Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ, τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν εἶναι κόσμου, ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως·

records.literal_gloss: Not for through law the promise to the Abraham or to the seed of him, the heir him to be of world, but through righteousness of faith;

en.L: For the promise to Abraham or to his seed, that he would be heir of [the] world, [was] not through [the] law but through [the] righteousness of faith;
en.B: The promise that he would inherit the world did not come to Abraham or to his offspring through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
en.R: God promised Abraham and his descendants that the whole world would belong to them. God did not make this promise because Abraham obeyed the law. God made it because of Abraham's faith, which God counted as righteousness.

es.L: Porque no por medio de [la] ley [fue] la promesa a Abraham o a su descendencia de que él sería heredero del mundo, sino por medio de [la] justicia de [la] fe;
es.B: La promesa de que heredaría el mundo no les llegó a Abraham ni a su descendencia por medio de la ley, sino por medio de la justicia de la fe.
es.R: Dios prometió a Abraham y a sus descendientes que el mundo entero sería de ellos. Dios no hizo esta promesa porque Abraham obedeciera la ley. La hizo por la fe de Abraham, que Dios le acreditó como justicia.

sw.L: Kwa maana ahadi kwa Ibrahimu au kwa uzao wake, kwamba yeye atakuwa mrithi wa ulimwengu, [haikuwa] kupitia sheria, bali kupitia haki ya imani;
sw.B: Ahadi kwamba angeurithi ulimwengu haikumjia Ibrahimu wala uzao wake kupitia sheria, bali kupitia haki ya imani.
sw.R: Mungu alimwahidi Ibrahimu na wazao wake kwamba ulimwengu wote utakuwa wao. Mungu hakutoa ahadi hii kwa sababu Ibrahimu aliitii sheria. Aliitoa kwa sababu ya imani ya Ibrahimu, ambayo Mungu aliihesabu kuwa haki.

fr.L: Car la promesse faite à Abraham ou à sa descendance, qu’il serait héritier du monde, [n’est] pas [venue] par [la] Loi, mais par [la] justice de [la] foi ;
fr.B: La promesse d’hériter du monde n’est pas venue à Abraham ou à sa descendance par la Loi, mais par la justice de la foi.
fr.R: Dieu a promis à Abraham et à ses descendants que le monde entier leur appartiendrait. Dieu n’a pas fait cette promesse parce qu’Abraham obéissait à la Loi. Dieu l’a faite à cause de la foi d’Abraham, que Dieu a comptée comme justice.

decisions.reason: God promised Abraham the land (Genesis 12:7, 15:18) and blessing for all the families of the earth through him (Genesis 12:3, 22:17-18). Jewish writings of the time already widened the promise to the whole earth (Sirach 44:21). Paul speaks of the world as the inheritance.

decisions.choice: through the law / through the righteousness of faith
decisions.reason: The promise came long before the law was given at Sinai (Galatians 3:17 counts 430 years). It rested on the righteousness God counted to Abraham's faith.
As in 9:7: the same word at each level throughout Romans.
As in 9:7, "descendencia" is the everyday collective word for offspring; Readable says "descendientes" as the English Readable says "descendants". Verses 16 and 18 follow.
As in 9:7, the collective "uzao" renders the singular "seed" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "wazao" (descendants). Verses 16 and 18 follow.

'Semence' and 'postérité' are the older words for offspring and are no longer current in this sense. 'Descendance' is the everyday collective word, singular like the Greek, and Readable says 'descendants', as the English Readable says 'descendants'.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι, κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία·

records.literal_gloss: If for those from law heirs, has been emptied the faith and has been nullified the promise;

en.L: For if those who are of [the] law [are] heirs, faith has been emptied and the promise nullified;
en.B: If the heirs are those who rely on the law, faith is made empty and the promise is worthless.
en.R: If people get what God promised by obeying the law, then faith means nothing, and God's promise is worthless.

es.L: Porque si los de [la] ley [son] herederos, la fe ha quedado vacía y la promesa ha sido anulada;
es.B: Si los herederos son los que se apoyan en la ley, la fe queda vacía y la promesa no vale nada.
es.R: Si la gente recibe lo que Dios prometió por obedecer la ley, entonces la fe no significa nada, y la promesa de Dios no vale nada.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa wale walio wa sheria [ndio] warithi, imani imefanywa tupu na ahadi imebatilishwa;
sw.B: Ikiwa warithi ni wale wanaotegemea sheria, imani inakuwa haina maana, na ahadi inakuwa haina thamani.
sw.R: Kama watu wanapata kile ambacho Mungu aliahidi kwa kuitii sheria, basi imani haina maana yoyote, na ahadi ya Mungu haina thamani.

fr.L: Car si ceux qui sont de [la] Loi [sont] héritiers, la foi a été vidée [de son sens] et la promesse annulée ;
fr.B: Si les héritiers sont ceux qui s’appuient sur la Loi, la foi est vidée de son sens et la promesse ne vaut plus rien.
fr.R: Si les gens reçoivent ce que Dieu a promis en obéissant à la Loi, alors la foi ne sert à rien, et la promesse de Dieu ne vaut rien.

decisions.choice: those of the law: those whose claim rests on the law
decisions.reason: "Of the law" describes people whose standing comes from the law. If the inheritance depended on that, a promise received by faith would mean nothing.

decisions.choice: los que se apoyan en la ley (B); anulada (L)
decisions.reason: "Los de la ley" is kept at Literal but is not natural prose; Balanced says "los que se apoyan en la ley" (those who rely on the law), the phrase of Galatians 3:10 for the same idea (meaning decision). Literal renders the second verb with "anular", as in 3:3 and 3:31, where it is the same verb.
This is the verb of 3:3 and 3:31, rendered there with "kubatilisha" (to make void), so Literal keeps it.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται, οὗ δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος, οὐδὲ παράβασις.

records.literal_gloss: The for law wrath brings about; where but not is law, neither transgression.

en.L: For the law brings about wrath; but where there is no law, neither [is there] transgression.
en.B: The law brings about wrath. But where there is no law, there is no breaking of the law either.
en.R: The law brings God's anger, because people break it. But where there is no law, no one can break it.

es.L: Porque la ley acarrea ira; pero donde no existe ley, tampoco [existe] transgresión.
es.B: La ley trae consigo la ira. Pero donde no hay ley, tampoco hay quebrantamiento de la ley.
es.R: La ley trae la ira de Dios, porque la gente la quebranta. Pero donde no hay ley, nadie puede quebrantarla.

sw.L: Kwa maana sheria huleta ghadhabu; lakini pasipo sheria, hapo hakuna ukiukaji [wa sheria] pia.
sw.B: Sheria huleta ghadhabu. Lakini mahali pasipo na sheria, hakuna kuivunja sheria pia.
sw.R: Sheria inaleta ghadhabu ya Mungu, kwa sababu watu huivunja. Lakini mahali ambapo hakuna sheria, hakuna mtu anayeweza kuivunja.

fr.L: Car la Loi produit la colère ; mais là où il n’y a pas de loi, il n’y a pas non plus de transgression.
fr.B: La Loi produit la colère. Mais là où il n’y a pas de loi, il n’y a pas non plus de désobéissance à la loi.
fr.R: La Loi attire la colère de Dieu, parce que les gens lui désobéissent. Mais là où il n’y a pas de loi, personne ne peut lui désobéir.

decisions.reason: As in 1:18 and 2:5, the wrath is God's judgment on wrongdoing.
As in 2:23. Without a law there is still sin (5:13), but not the breaking of a command.
Readable says how the law brings wrath, as the second half of the verse implies.
As in 1:18.

decisions.choice: ira (every level); transgresión (L), quebrantamiento de la ley (B)
decisions.reason: As in 1:18, Spanish "ira" is an everyday word, so Readable keeps the key term ("la ira de Dios") where the English Readable says "God's anger". For breaking a known command Literal says "transgresión", as in 2:23, and Balanced and Readable "quebrantar" (to break), as the English does.

decisions.choice: ghadhabu (every level); ukiukaji [wa sheria] (L), kuivunja sheria (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:18, "ghadhabu" is the settled word for God's wrath and is well known, so Readable keeps it ("ghadhabu ya Mungu"); "hasira" is ordinary human anger. For breaking a command Literal says "ukiukaji", as "kukiuka" in 2:23, and Balanced and Readable "kuivunja" (break it).

source.text: Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως, ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι, οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν, καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε, κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα·

records.literal_gloss: Because of this from faith, that according to grace, for the to be firm the promise to all the seed, not to the [one] from the law only but also to the [one] from faith of Abraham, who is father of all of us, \v 17 as it has been written that: Father of many nations I have made you, before whom he believed God the [one] giving life to the dead and calling the [things] not being as being;

en.L: For this reason [it is] by faith, so that [it may be] by grace, so that the promise may be sure to all the seed, not only to the [seed] of the law but also to the [seed] of the faith of Abraham, who is [the] father of us all, \v 17 as it is written, "I have made you [the] father of many nations," before the God whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls the things that do not exist as existing;
en.B: So the promise comes through faith, in order that it may rest on grace and stand firm for every one of Abraham's offspring: not only for those who belong to the law, but also for those who belong to the faith of Abraham, the father of all of us. \v 17 Scripture says, "I have made you father of many nations." Before God he is our father, the God he believed, who brings the dead to life and calls into being things that do not exist.
en.R: That is why God's promise comes through faith. It is God's gift of grace, and so it is sure for all of Abraham's descendants. It is not only for those who have the law. It is also for those who have faith as Abraham did. He is the father of all of us who believe. \v 17 As the Scriptures say, God told him, "I have made you the father of many nations." Abraham is our father in the sight of God, the God he believed. God gives life to the dead. He speaks, and things that did not exist come into being.

es.L: Por esto [es] por fe, para que [sea] conforme a [la] gracia, a fin de que la promesa sea firme para toda la descendencia, no solo para la [que es] de la ley, sino también para la [que es] de la fe de Abraham, quien es padre de todos nosotros, \v 17 según está escrito: «Te he hecho padre de muchas naciones», delante del Dios en quien creyó, el que da vida a los muertos y llama a lo que no existe como existente;
es.B: Por eso la promesa viene por la fe, para que descanse en la gracia y quede firme para toda la descendencia de Abraham: no solo para los que pertenecen a la ley, sino también para los que pertenecen a la fe de Abraham, el padre de todos nosotros. \v 17 La Escritura dice: «Te he hecho padre de muchas naciones». Ante Dios él es nuestro padre, el Dios en quien creyó, que da vida a los muertos y llama a la existencia lo que no existe.
es.R: Por eso la promesa de Dios viene por medio de la fe. Es un regalo de la gracia de Dios, y por eso es segura para todos los descendientes de Abraham. No es solo para los que tienen la ley. Es también para los que tienen fe como la tuvo Abraham. Él es el padre de todos los que creemos. \v 17 Como dicen las Escrituras, Dios le dijo: «Te he hecho padre de muchas naciones». Abraham es nuestro padre a los ojos de Dios, el Dios en quien creyó. Dios da vida a los muertos. Habla, y lo que no existía comienza a existir.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hii [ni] kwa imani, ili [iwe] kwa kadiri ya neema, ili ahadi iwe thabiti kwa uzao wote, si kwa ule [uzao] wa sheria peke yake, bali pia kwa ule wa imani ya Ibrahimu, ambaye ni baba yetu sisi sote, \v 17 kama ilivyoandikwa: "Nimekufanya kuwa baba wa mataifa mengi," mbele ya Mungu ambaye alimwamini, yule anayewapa wafu uzima na kuviita vitu visivyokuwako kana kwamba vipo;
sw.B: Kwa hiyo ahadi inakuja kwa imani, ili itegemee neema na iwe imara kwa uzao wote wa Ibrahimu: si kwa wale walio wa sheria tu, bali pia kwa wale walio wa imani ya Ibrahimu, baba yetu sote. \v 17 Maandiko yanasema, "Nimekufanya kuwa baba wa mataifa mengi." Mbele za Mungu yeye ni baba yetu, Mungu yule aliyemwamini, anayewapa wafu uzima na kuviita viwepo vitu visivyokuwepo.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu ahadi ya Mungu inakuja kwa imani. Ni zawadi ya neema ya Mungu, na kwa hiyo ni ya hakika kwa wazao wote wa Ibrahimu. Si kwa wale walio na sheria tu. Ni pia kwa wale walio na imani kama Ibrahimu. Yeye ni baba yetu sisi sote tunaoamini. \v 17 Kama Maandiko yasemavyo, Mungu alimwambia, "Nimekufanya kuwa baba wa mataifa mengi." Ibrahimu ni baba yetu machoni pa Mungu, Mungu yule aliyemwamini. Mungu huwapa wafu uzima. Husema, na vitu ambavyo havikuwepo vinakuwepo.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi [c’est] par [la] foi, afin que [ce soit] par grâce, pour que la promesse soit assurée à toute la descendance, non seulement à celle [qui est] de la Loi, mais aussi à celle [qui est] de la foi d’Abraham, qui est [le] père de nous tous, \v 17 comme il est écrit : « Je t’ai établi père de nombreuses nations », devant le Dieu auquel il a cru, qui donne la vie aux morts et appelle les choses qui ne sont pas comme si elles étaient ;
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi la promesse vient par la foi : afin qu’elle repose sur la grâce et qu’elle soit assurée pour toute la descendance d’Abraham, non seulement pour ceux qui relèvent de la Loi, mais aussi pour ceux qui relèvent de la foi d’Abraham, le père de nous tous. \v 17 L’Écriture dit : « Je t’ai fait père de nombreuses nations. » Devant Dieu, il est notre père, devant le Dieu auquel il a cru, qui fait revivre les morts et appelle à l’existence ce qui n’existe pas.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi la promesse de Dieu vient par la foi. C’est un don de la grâce de Dieu, et ainsi elle est sûre pour tous les descendants d’Abraham. Elle n’est pas seulement pour ceux qui ont la Loi. Elle est aussi pour ceux qui ont la foi, comme Abraham. Il est le père de nous tous qui croyons. \v 17 Comme le disent les Écritures, Dieu lui a dit : « J’ai fait de toi le père de nombreuses nations. » Abraham est notre père aux yeux de Dieu, le Dieu auquel il a cru. Dieu donne la vie aux morts. Il parle, et ce qui n’existait pas se met à exister.

decisions.reason: "I have made you the father of many nations" is Genesis 17:5, where God changes Abram's name to Abraham.

decisions.choice: the seed of the law and the seed of faith
decisions.reason: Both groups are believers: Jewish believers, who have the law, and Gentile believers, who share Abraham's faith without it. Verse 14 has already ruled out the law alone as the ground of inheritance.

decisions.choice: calls into being what does not exist
alternatives: speaks of what does not yet exist as though it did
decisions.reason: The phrase can describe God's creating word, as in creation, or his naming of what is still to come, as he named Abraham father of nations before he had a son. Paired with "gives life to the dead", it most likely speaks of God's power to create.

decisions.choice: before the God whom he believed
decisions.reason: The Greek is compressed: "before whom he believed, God". Abraham is father of all believers in God's sight, whatever his descent.
As in verse 13.
The verb is "make alive", not the usual verb for raising, so Swahili says "gives life to the dead" with "uzima", the settled word for life.

source.text: ὃς παρ’ ἐλπίδα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου·

records.literal_gloss: Who against hope on hope believed for the to become him father of many nations according to the having been spoken: So will be the seed of you;

en.L: who against hope believed in hope, so that he became [the] father of many nations, according to what had been spoken, "So will your seed be";
en.B: Hoping when there was no ground for hope, Abraham believed, and so he became the father of many nations, as God had said to him, "That is how many your offspring will be."
en.R: There was no reason to hope, but Abraham hoped and believed. And so he became the father of many nations, as God had told him: "Your descendants will be as many as the stars."

es.L: quien contra [toda] esperanza creyó con esperanza, de modo que llegó a ser padre de muchas naciones, según lo que había sido dicho: «Así será tu descendencia»;
es.B: Esperando cuando no había razón para esperar, Abraham creyó, y así llegó a ser padre de muchas naciones, como Dios le había dicho: «Así de numerosa será tu descendencia».
es.R: No había razón para tener esperanza, pero Abraham esperó y creyó. Y así llegó a ser el padre de muchas naciones, como Dios le había dicho: «Tus descendientes serán tantos como las estrellas».

sw.L: ambaye kinyume cha tumaini aliamini katika tumaini, hata akawa baba wa mataifa mengi, kwa kadiri ya kile kilichonenwa: "Uzao wako utakuwa hivyo";
sw.B: Akitumaini wakati hapakuwa na sababu ya kutumaini, Ibrahimu aliamini, na hivyo akawa baba wa mataifa mengi, kama Mungu alivyokuwa amemwambia: "Hivyo ndivyo uzao wako utakavyokuwa mwingi."
sw.R: Hapakuwa na sababu ya kutumaini, lakini Ibrahimu alitumaini na kuamini. Na hivyo akawa baba wa mataifa mengi, kama Mungu alivyomwambia: "Wazao wako watakuwa wengi kama nyota."

fr.L: lui qui, contre [toute] espérance, a cru avec espérance, de sorte qu’il est devenu [le] père de nombreuses nations, selon ce qui avait été dit : « Ainsi sera ta descendance » ;
fr.B: Espérant alors qu’il n’y avait aucune raison d’espérer, Abraham a cru, et ainsi il est devenu le père de nombreuses nations, comme Dieu le lui avait dit : « Ta descendance sera aussi nombreuse. »
fr.R: Il n’y avait aucune raison d’espérer, mais Abraham a espéré et il a cru. Et c’est ainsi qu’il est devenu le père de nombreuses nations, comme Dieu le lui avait dit : « Tes descendants seront aussi nombreux que les étoiles. »

decisions.reason: God took Abraham outside, told him to count the stars, and said, "So will your offspring be" (Genesis 15:5).
A play on words: when all human reason for hope was gone, Abraham hoped in God.

decisions.choice: so that he became: the result, and God's purpose
decisions.reason: The construction gives the outcome of his believing, which was also what God intended.
Readable includes the stars from Genesis 15:5, since "so" means "as many as the stars".
The play on words (meaning decision) needs "esperanza" twice; Literal brackets "toda" to make "against hope" clear in Spanish, and keeps the verb "creyó" of the Greek.

decisions.choice: kinyume cha tumaini ... katika tumaini (L); kutumaini (B, R)
decisions.reason: The play on words (meaning decision) needs one word twice, so every level repeats "tumaini" (hope) in noun or verb.

decisions.choice: contre [toute] espérance, a cru avec espérance
decisions.reason: The play on words (meaning decision) needs 'espérance' twice; Literal brackets 'toute' to make 'against hope' clear in French.

source.text: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας, εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And not having weakened in the faith he considered the of himself body having been made dead, a hundred years old about being, and the deadness of the womb of Sarah, \v 20 at but the promise of the God not he doubted in the unbelief but was strengthened in the faith, having given glory to the God \v 21 and having been fully convinced that what he has promised able he is also to do.

en.L: And without weakening in faith he considered his own body, already as good as dead (since he was about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah's womb; \v 20 yet with respect to the promise of God he did not waver in unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God, \v 21 and being fully convinced that what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was able also to do.
en.B: His faith did not weaken when he looked at his own body, as good as dead now that he was about a hundred years old, or at the deadness of Sarah's womb. \v 20 He did not doubt God's promise or waver in unbelief. Instead he grew strong in faith and gave glory to God, \v 21 fully convinced that God had the power to carry out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised.
en.R: Abraham was about a hundred years old, and his body was as good as dead. His wife Sarah was too old to have children. Abraham knew this, but his faith did not become weak. \v 20 He did not stop believing God's promise. Instead, his faith grew stronger, and he gave glory to God. \v 21 He was completely sure that God could do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised.

es.L: Y sin debilitarse en la fe, consideró su propio cuerpo, ya como muerto (pues tenía unos cien años), y el vientre de Sara, ya sin vida; \v 20 pero respecto a la promesa de Dios no vaciló con incredulidad, sino que fue fortalecido en la fe, dando gloria a Dios, \v 21 y estando plenamente convencido de que lo que había prometido, también era poderoso para hacerlo.
es.B: Su fe no se debilitó cuando miró su propio cuerpo, que ya estaba como muerto porque tenía unos cien años, ni cuando pensó en el vientre de Sara, ya sin vida. \v 20 No dudó de la promesa de Dios ni vaciló por falta de fe. Al contrario, su fe se hizo fuerte, y dio gloria a Dios, \v 21 pues estaba totalmente convencido de que Dios tenía poder para cumplir lo que había prometido.
es.R: Abraham tenía unos cien años, y su cuerpo estaba ya como muerto. Su esposa Sara era demasiado anciana para tener hijos. Abraham lo sabía, pero su fe no se debilitó. \v 20 No dejó de creer en la promesa de Dios. Al contrario, su fe se hizo más fuerte, y dio gloria a Dios. \v 21 Estaba completamente seguro de que Dios podía hacer lo que había prometido.

sw.L: Na bila kudhoofika katika imani, aliutafakari mwili wake mwenyewe, uliokuwa kama umekufa tayari (kwa kuwa alikuwa na umri wa karibu miaka mia moja), na tumbo la uzazi la Sara lililokuwa limekufa; \v 20 lakini kuhusu ahadi ya Mungu hakusitasita kwa kutoamini, bali aliimarishwa katika imani, akimpa Mungu utukufu, \v 21 na akiwa amesadiki kabisa kwamba kile alichoahidi, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anaweza pia kukitenda.
sw.B: Imani yake haikudhoofika alipoutazama mwili wake, uliokuwa kama umekufa kwa kuwa alikuwa na umri wa karibu miaka mia moja, wala alipofikiria tumbo la Sara lililokuwa limekufa. \v 20 Hakuwa na shaka juu ya ahadi ya Mungu, wala hakusitasita kwa kutoamini. Badala yake imani yake ilipata nguvu, akampa Mungu utukufu, \v 21 akiwa na hakika kamili kwamba Mungu ana uwezo wa kutimiza kile alichoahidi.
sw.R: Ibrahimu alikuwa na umri wa karibu miaka mia moja, na mwili wake ulikuwa kama umekufa. Mke wake Sara alikuwa mzee mno kuweza kuzaa watoto. Ibrahimu alijua jambo hili, lakini imani yake haikudhoofika. \v 20 Hakuacha kuiamini ahadi ya Mungu. Badala yake, imani yake ilizidi kuwa na nguvu, naye akampa Mungu utukufu. \v 21 Alikuwa na hakika kabisa kwamba Mungu angeweza kufanya kile alichoahidi.

fr.L: Et, sans faiblir dans la foi, il a considéré son propre corps déjà comme mort (il avait environ cent ans) et le sein de Sara, frappé de mort ; \v 20 mais à l’égard de la promesse de Dieu, il n’a pas hésité par incrédulité, mais il a été fortifié par la foi, donnant gloire à Dieu \v 21 et étant pleinement convaincu que ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait promis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était capable aussi de le faire.
fr.B: Sa foi n’a pas faibli quand il a regardé son propre corps, déjà comme mort puisqu’il avait environ cent ans, ni le sein de Sara, frappé de mort. \v 20 Il n’a pas douté de la promesse de Dieu et n’a pas hésité par incrédulité. Au contraire, il s’est fortifié dans la foi et il a rendu gloire à Dieu, \v 21 pleinement convaincu que Dieu avait la puissance d’accomplir ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait promis.
fr.R: Abraham avait environ cent ans, et son corps était comme mort. Sa femme Sara était trop âgée pour avoir des enfants. Abraham le savait, mais sa foi n’a pas faibli. \v 20 Il n’a pas cessé de croire à la promesse de Dieu. Au contraire, sa foi est devenue plus forte, et il a rendu gloire à Dieu. \v 21 Il était tout à fait sûr que Dieu pouvait faire ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait promis.

alternatives: many manuscripts read "he did not consider his own body"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "not". In the SBLGNT text Abraham faces the facts and believes anyway; in the other reading he does not dwell on them. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)
διακρίνω here is to be torn between belief and unbelief.
Abraham did what humanity failed to do in 1:21: he gave God glory and trusted his power.

decisions.choice: Paul looks at Abraham's faith as a whole
decisions.reason: Genesis records that Abraham laughed at the promise (Genesis 17:17). Paul speaks of the faith that held through it, which God counted as righteousness.

decisions.choice: Sarah was too old to have children
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the phrase means.

decisions.choice: dando gloria a Dios (L); dio gloria a Dios (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision sets Abraham against 1:21, where people did not give God glory. Spanish Balanced says "dar gloria" there, so every level here uses the same words and the contrast can be seen.

decisions.choice: fue fortalecido (L); su fe se hizo fuerte (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is passive: Abraham was made strong. Literal keeps the passive.

decisions.choice: akimpa Mungu utukufu (L); akampa Mungu utukufu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision sets Abraham against 1:21, where Balanced says "hawakumpa utukufu" (they did not give him glory). Every level here uses the same words, so the contrast can be seen. Balanced has no deity pronoun span where the English has one: Swahili marks the pronoun inside the verb ("alichoahidi").

decisions.choice: donnant gloire à Dieu (L); a rendu gloire à Dieu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision sets Abraham against 1:21, where people did not give God glory. French Balanced and Readable say 'rendre gloire' there, so every level here uses the same words and the contrast can be seen.

source.text: διὸ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore it was counted to him for righteousness.

en.L: Therefore "it was counted to him as righteousness."
en.B: That is why "it was counted to him as righteousness."
en.R: That is why God counted his faith as righteousness.

es.L: Por lo cual «le fue acreditado como justicia».
es.B: Por eso «se le acreditó como justicia».
es.R: Por eso Dios le acreditó su fe como justicia.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo "lilihesabiwa kwake kuwa haki."
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu "lilihesabiwa kwake kuwa haki."
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu Mungu aliihesabu imani yake kuwa haki.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi « cela lui a été compté comme justice ».
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi « cela lui a été compté comme justice ».
fr.R: C’est pourquoi Dieu a compté sa foi comme justice.

decisions.reason: Paul repeats the words of Genesis 15:6 from verse 3.
λογίζομαι comes eleven times in this chapter. The same English is kept wherever it can be, so that the thread of Paul's argument stays visible, as in 9:8.

source.text: Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ δι’ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ, ἀλλὰ καὶ δι’ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν, ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Not was written but because of him only that it was counted to him, \v 24 but also because of us, to whom it is about to be counted, to those believing on the [one] having raised Jesus the Lord of us from dead, \v 25 who was handed over because of the trespasses of us and was raised because of the justification of us.

en.L: Now it was not written for his sake alone that it was counted to him, \v 24 but also for our sake, to whom it will be counted, who believe in the one who raised Jesus our Lord from [the] dead, \v 25 who was handed over for our trespasses and was raised for our justification.
en.B: The words "it was counted to him" were not written for Abraham alone, \v 24 but for us as well. It will be counted to us who believe in the God who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead. \v 25 Jesus was handed over to die because of our trespasses, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was raised so that we would be declared righteous.
en.R: The words "God counted it to him" were not written only for Abraham. \v 24 They were also written for us. God will count us as righteous too, all of us who believe in the God who raised Jesus our Lord from death. \v 25 Jesus was handed over to die because of our sins. And God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to life to make us right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

es.L: Ahora bien, no se escribió solo por causa de él que le fue acreditado, \v 24 sino también por causa de nosotros, a quienes nos será acreditado, a los que creemos en el que resucitó de entre [los] muertos a Jesús nuestro Señor, \v 25 quien fue entregado a causa de nuestras transgresiones y fue resucitado a causa de nuestra justificación.
es.B: Las palabras «se le acreditó» no se escribieron solo para Abraham, \v 24 sino también para nosotros. Se nos acreditará a nosotros, los que creemos en el Dios que resucitó de entre los muertos a Jesús nuestro Señor. \v 25 Jesús fue entregado a la muerte a causa de nuestras transgresiones, y fue resucitado para que fuéramos justificados.
es.R: Las palabras «Dios se lo acreditó» no se escribieron solo para Abraham. \v 24 También se escribieron para nosotros. Dios también nos considerará justos a nosotros, a todos los que creemos en el Dios que resucitó a Jesús nuestro Señor de la muerte. \v 25 Jesús fue entregado a la muerte por nuestros pecados. Y Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} resucitó para declararnos justos.

sw.L: Basi haikuandikwa kwa ajili yake peke yake kwamba lilihesabiwa kwake, \v 24 bali pia kwa ajili yetu, ambao litahesabiwa kwetu, sisi tunaomwamini yule aliyemfufua Yesu Bwana wetu kutoka kwa wafu, \v 25 ambaye alitolewa kwa sababu ya makosa yetu, na akafufuliwa kwa sababu ya kuhesabiwa haki kwetu.
sw.B: Maneno "lilihesabiwa kwake" hayakuandikwa kwa ajili ya Ibrahimu peke yake, \v 24 bali kwa ajili yetu pia. Litahesabiwa kwetu sisi tunaomwamini Mungu aliyemfufua Yesu Bwana wetu kutoka kwa wafu. \v 25 Yesu alitolewa afe kwa sababu ya makosa yetu, naye akafufuliwa ili sisi tupate kuhesabiwa haki.
sw.R: Maneno "Mungu alimhesabia hilo" hayakuandikwa kwa ajili ya Ibrahimu peke yake. \v 24 Yaliandikwa pia kwa ajili yetu. Mungu atatuhesabu sisi pia kuwa wenye haki, sisi sote tunaomwamini Mungu aliyemfufua Yesu Bwana wetu kutoka kwa wafu. \v 25 Yesu alitolewa afe kwa sababu ya dhambi zetu. Na Mungu alimfufua ili atuhesabie haki.

fr.L: Or ce n’est pas pour lui seul qu’il a été écrit que cela lui a été compté, \v 24 mais aussi pour nous, à qui cela sera compté, nous qui croyons en celui qui a ressuscité d’entre [les] morts Jésus notre Seigneur, \v 25 {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui a été livré à cause de nos fautes et a été ressuscité à cause de notre justification.
fr.B: Les mots « cela lui a été compté » n’ont pas été écrits pour Abraham seul, \v 24 mais aussi pour nous. Cela nous sera compté, à nous qui croyons en Dieu qui a ressuscité d’entre les morts Jésus notre Seigneur. \v 25 Jésus a été livré à la mort à cause de nos fautes, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été ressuscité pour que nous soyons justifiés.
fr.R: Les mots « Dieu le lui a compté » n’ont pas été écrits seulement pour Abraham. \v 24 Ils ont aussi été écrits pour nous. Dieu nous comptera comme justes, nous aussi, nous tous qui croyons en Dieu, qui a ressuscité Jésus notre Seigneur d’entre les morts. \v 25 Jésus a été livré à la mort à cause de nos péchés. Et Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ramené à la vie pour nous déclarer justes.

decisions.reason: "Handed over because of our trespasses" echoes the Greek translation of Isaiah 53:12, where the servant of the LORD "was handed over because of their sins".

decisions.choice: because of our trespasses; for our justification
decisions.reason: The same preposition is used twice. The first looks back (our trespasses were the reason he was handed over); the second looks forward (he was raised to bring about our being declared righteous).
The verb looks forward: righteousness is counted to everyone who believes, and will be confirmed at the judgment.
The passive leaves God as the one who handed him over, as 8:32 says, using the same verb as 1:24.
λογίζομαι comes eleven times in this chapter. The same English is kept wherever it can be, so that the thread of Paul's argument stays visible, as in 9:8.
Balanced and Readable say what he was handed over to.

decisions.choice: a causa de ... a causa de (L); a causa de ... para que fuéramos justificados (B); por ... para declararnos justos (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that one preposition is used twice, looking back and then forward. Literal keeps one Spanish phrase for both, as the English Literal keeps "for"; Balanced and Readable show that the second looks forward. "Transgresiones" renders "trespasses", as in 11:11; Readable says "pecados", as the English Readable says "sins".
Where a person is counted as righteous, Readable says "considerar justo", as in verses 6 and 11.

decisions.choice: kwa sababu ya makosa yetu ... kwa sababu ya kuhesabiwa haki kwetu (L); ili sisi tupate kuhesabiwa haki (B); ili atuhesabie haki (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that one preposition is used twice, looking back and then forward. Literal keeps "kwa sababu ya" for both; Balanced and Readable show that the second looks forward with "ili" (so that). "Makosa" renders "trespasses", as "kosa" in 11:11. The noun for justification is said with the settled "kuhesabiwa haki". Readable has no deity pronoun span where the English has one: the object is marked in the verb ("alimfufua").

decisions.choice: à cause de ... à cause de (L); à cause de ... pour que (B); à cause de ... pour (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that one preposition is used twice, looking back and then forward. Literal keeps one French phrase for both, as the English Literal keeps 'for'; Balanced and Readable show the second as a purpose, as the English does.
